title: Auriga - POC scoping (open model shortlist)
next_steps: Send benchmark spreadsheet and recommended model shortlist (Aaron) by 2026-12-20
Schedule 60-min technical deep dive with Auriga infra team (Priya) in next week
Share SOC2 + security pack and SSO integration guide (Aaron)
Kickoff 6-week POC once legal/PO approved: target start 2027-01-04
action_items: Aaron: share baseline benchmark spreadsheet and initial cost estimate (due 2026-12-20)
Priya: set up short demo of KV caching and quantization flow for Auriga (due 2026-12-23)
Mateo: provide 1k-sample anonymized test prompts and a gold-set for eval (due 2026-12-22)
Samir: confirm network egress constraints and preferred VPC peering window (due 2026-12-21)
summary: POC scoping focused on selecting an open-model shortlist for a 6-week pilot. Customer cares about multilingual support (EN/ES/FR), biomedical domain accuracy, latency under 200ms p50 for interactive workflows, and cost predictability. Redwood proposed candidate models, discussed quantization and KV-cache tradeoffs, and agreed next steps: send benchmarks, security docs, schedule infra deep dive, and start POC early Jan.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Aaron (AE, Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick rolL call, I'm Aaron, AE on the account, with Priya and Jonah from eng. Lina, Mateo, Samir, Eve - thanks for joining.
[00:00:18] Lina (PM, Auriga): Hi all, thanks. We're excited to scope a POC for integrating an open model for our clinical summarization product. Key constraints are accuracy on biomedical notes, plus Spanish and French support.
[00:00:35] Aaron: Great. Quick agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, model shortlist, benchmarks, timeline. We'll surface tradeoffs between quality, latency, and cost.
[00:00:48] Priya (SE): A note — we'll talk about quantizashun and KV caching since those materially change latency/cost. Also deployment modes: Hosted API vs Redwood Dedicated vs Private VPC.
[00:01:05] Mateo (ML Eng): For us accuracy is top; we need recall on key entities (meds, dosages, allergies). Target F1 improvements vs current baseline (our baseline is a finetuned 7B open model) — we want at least +6-8% on our eval set.
[00:01:22] Samir (Infra): And from infra we need to know latency SLOs and network constraints. We have strict egress rules from our VPC, may need private deployment or peered connection.
[00:01:35] Aaron: Noted. Can we run through success criteria? Lina?
[00:01:40] Lina: Sure — 1) quality: domain-specific accuracy targets (F1 +6-8), 2) latency: p50 <200ms for interactive summarization on short notes (~150 tokens), 3) cost: predictable per-inference cost to fit our CP budget, 4) multilingual: reasonable quality for ES/FR, 5) security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS.
[00:02:05] Priya: Good set. For timelines, we typically do a 6-week POC: week 0 onboarding & infra, week 1 baseline benchmarks, week 2 integration w/ retrieval, week 3 domain eval & tuning, week 4 iterate, week 5 production smoke & ops handoff, week 6 wrap and decision. Does that align?
[00:02:23] Eve (CTO): That's reasonable. We likely need procurement sign-off first but aim to start early Jan.
[00:02:30] Jonah: On workload sizing — can you share expected qps and typical payload sizes?
[00:02:36] Mateo: Typical interactive rate per user is 0.2 qps, peak concurrency ~40 users, expect 8-10k API calls per day for the pilot. Average prompt + context ~350 tokens, output ~150 tokens. We'll provide sample logs.
[00:02:55] Priya: Okay that helps. For benchmarking we'll recommend a shortlist of open models spanning cost/quality: Llama 3 7B and 13B, Mistral-Instruct (7B), Falcon-40B-instruct, MPT-30B-instruct, and a smaller tuned Llama2-13B variant. We'll include quantized variants (4-bit int4/int8) where supported.
[00:03:20] Mateo: Curious about multilingual — we have important Spanish & French content, and occasional Portuguese. Which of those models perform well out-of-the-box?
[00:03:26] Priya: In our experience, Llama 3 and Mistral tend to generalize well in ES/FR; Falcon 40B strong in EN but mixed on other lang's unless finetuned. MPT has decent tokenizer coverage for Romance languages. We'll validate with your gold-set.
[00:03:45] Samir: Any license concerns? We prefer permissive licenses for production.
[00:03:50] Aaron: We'll flag license notes in the sheet. Some weights have usage restrictions — we'll call those out (e.g., commercial terms).
[00:03:58] Lina: Benchmarks — what metrics will Redwood run?
[00:04:02] Priya: We'll run p50/p95 latency on your target infra (we can run in our hosted infra and also on Dedicated sim), token throughput, cost per 1k outputs, and domain accuracy (F1/EM) against your gold-set. Also memory/kv-cache footprint for long context retrieval.
[00:04:20] Mateo: For domain accuracy, we want evaluation both with and without retrieval augmentation — retrieval is core to our pipeline.
[00:04:27] Priya: Yep, we'll test both: pure model vs model+retrieval (we'll simulate your vector DB or use your repo samples). We'll capture delta in accuracy and cost.
[00:04:36] Aaron: Quick note on KV cache — for conversational flows it saves repeated prefix compute and drastically improves throughput for multi-turn. For summarization it's less impactful but helps if you have repeated system context.
[00:04:49] Samir: How big is that complexity to enable?
[00:04:52] Priya: It's straightforward on Redwood runtime; we'll show a demo. Some kernels/quantizations interact with KV cache — we'll test combos.
[00:04:59] Lina: On quantization — we worry about quality regressions.
[00:05:02] Priya: Totally. In general: int8/4 quant gives big cost wins; for some models quality drop is negligible on classification/completion tasks, but for domain-sensitive extraction you may see edge cases. We'll quantify per-model.
[00:05:17] Jonah: Can Redwood run a head-to-head on our subset and give a recommendation?
[00:05:21] Aaron: Yes — we'll run head-to-heads and present a short recommended shortlist with expected cost/latency/quality tradeoffs. We'll probably recommend two tracks: a lower-latency smaller model (Llama3-7B/Mistral7B quantized) for interactive, and a higher-quality mid-sized model (Llama3-13B or MPT-30B or Falcon-40B depending on biomedical metrics) for batch or high-quality outputs.
[00:05:44] Mateo: Any issues with tokenization for clinical abbreviations? We have specialized tokens.
[00:05:49] Priya: Tokenization differences can matter. If you have a tokenizer map or a list of frequent abbreviations, share it. We can also test adding custom tokens in a finetune step if needed.
[00:05:59] Lina: For the POC success criteria, can we lock on exact thresholds?
[00:06:02] Aaron: Proposal: quality target = +6-8% F1 vs baseline on your gold-set; latency p50 <200ms on Redwood Dedicated / Hosted default with quantization and batching; cost: target <$0.03 per inference (TBD after model pick). We'll put ranges in the sheet.
[00:06:18] Samir: That latency target assumes what hardware?
[00:06:21] Priya: We'll profile on a single A100-like instance and a cheaper T4-equivalent to show tails. We'll include Dedicated pool configs.
[00:06:31] Eve: Security — we'll need SOC2 docs and KMS integration. Also we prefer not to send PHI off-site without a BAA conversation.
[00:06:39] Aaron: We'll share SOC2 and security pack. For PHI, we can discuss a Private deployment or dedicated tenancy and BAA. We'll flag that as part of procurement.
[00:06:48] Mateo: On tooling, we need to reproduce evals and line up dashboards.
[00:06:51] Jonah: Redwood Console will surface token cost, latency per model, per-route dashboards; we'll set a dedicated project for Auriga so you can see rollouts and trace hooks.
[00:06:59] Lina: Great. About multilingual evaluation — we'll provide 500 ES and 500 FR prompts for the initial eval.
[00:07:05] Priya: Perfect. We'll include those in the benchmark run and report per-language breakdown.
[00:07:10] Samir: Network — we need to confirm egress policy; if we can't allow outbound we may need Private. We'll get you windows for VPC peering.
[00:07:18] Aaron: Action: Samir will confirm constraints and preferred peering dates.
[00:07:23] Lina: On model shortlist, can you give quick pro/con bullets?
[00:07:27] Priya: Sure — Llama 3 7B: good latency, strong multilingual, cheap when quantized. Llama 3 13B: higher quality, higher cost, still good for ES/FR. Mistral-Instruct 7B: punchy, good for instruction tasks, strong cost/quality. MPT-30B: good for domain tasks, slower and larger. Falcon-40B: top-tier in some benchmarks but heavy to run, may need bigger infra and has mixed multilingual without finetune.
[00:07:56] Mateo: For biomedical, do you expect a 13B to close the gap vs our tuned 7B baseline?
[00:08:01] Priya: Possibly. Often a mid-sized 13B or a 30B with task-specific tuning + retrieval performs best. We'll run the head-to-head.
[00:08:09] Aaron: We'll include a column for finetune vs retrieval-only vs prompt-engineer approaches and delta on quality and cost.
[00:08:17] Lina: Timeline check — procurement sign-off target this week, POC start early Jan, final decision mid-Feb?
[00:08:23] Eve: yes that's our cadence.
[00:08:26] Aaron: Ok, logistics: I'll send the benchmark spreadsheet with these columns: model, hardware, quantization, p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k, domain F1, multilingual breakdown, notes on license. Expect that by Monday.
[00:08:40] Mateo: We'll anonymize and drop a 1k sample and gold-set into a shared S3 link.
[00:08:45] Priya: For the POC we'll recommend an initial run of 5 models across Hosted/Dedicated configs and pick the top 2 to iterate on.
[00:08:53] Samir: Can you run one baseline on our on-prem like VM? We can grant a temporary test node but need setup details.
[00:08:59] Priya: We'll outline RAM/GPU requirements. For heavier models like Falcon-40B, you'll need a 40-80GB GPU. We'll put hardware suggestions in the sheet.
[00:09:10] Lina: Anything else?
[00:09:12] Jonah: Quick reminder: sometimes tokenization or prompt length differences create hidden cost — we'll track average token counts pre/post.
[00:09:18] Aaron: Good. Recap of agreed next steps: Aaron sends benchmark sheet and security docs; Priya schedules technical deep dive with Samir; Auriga shares sample prompts and gold-set; technical infra checks for peering.
[00:09:33] Eve: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[00:09:35] Aaron: Thanks — we'll follow up with a calendar invite and artifacts.
[00:09:40] [call ends]

Note: transcription has occasional mis-hearings ("K V cash" for KV cache, "quantizashun"), some speaker labels simplified. References: benchmark spreadsheet: https://redwood.example.com/shared/auriga-redwood-benchmarks.xlsx ; security pack link: https://redwood.example.com/security/auriga-pack.zip
